case_name: Arindam Chattopadhyay And Others v State Of West Bengal And Others
facts: The appellants, who have been working as Child Development Project Officer (CDPO) in the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) since July, 1999, are entitled to be paid salary in the pay scale prescribed for that post.
On being selected by the West Bengal Public Service Commission, the appellants were appointed as Assistant Child Development Project Officer (ACDPO) in 1986-87.

After about 12 years, the competent authority issued order dated 7.7.1999 with the concurrence of the Finance Department of the Government whereby the petitioners were temporarily transferred to ICDS projects to act as CDPOs in their existing pay scales.

The appellants made representation dated 15.2.2011 with the prayer that they may either be promoted to the post of CDPO or be given pay scale of that post by asserting that they had been discharging the duties of the post of CDPO.
issues: Whether the appellants are entitled to be paid salary in the pay scale prescribed for the post of CDPO

Whether the stipulation contained in order dated 7.7.1999 that the appellants are temporarily transferred to ICDS project to act as CDPOs in their existing pay scale can be made the basis for depriving them of their constitutional right guaranteed under Arts. 14 and 16
petitioner_arguments: The doctrine of equality enshrined in Arts. 14 and 16 read with Art. 39(d) guarantees the appellants' constitutional right to be paid salary and allowances in the scale meant for the post of CDPO because they are discharging the duties of that post.
The stipulation contained in order dated 7.7.1999 cannot be made the basis for depriving them of their constitutional right guaranteed under Arts. 14 and 16.
respondent_arguments: The post of CDPO does not have any particular pay scale
Once the petitioners were asked to man the post temporarily, it would mean officiation in a superior post that would attract appropriate officiating allowance.
Pay scale in the superior post can only be achieved once they are promoted or absorbed in such post on promotional basis.
court_reasoning: The doctrine of equality enshrined in Arts. 14 and 16 read with Art. 39(d) guarantees the appellants' constitutional right to be paid salary and allowances in the scale meant for the post of CDPO because they are discharging the duties of that post.
The stipulation contained in order dated 7.7.1999 cannot be made the basis for depriving them of their constitutional right guaranteed under Arts. 14 and 16.
holding: The appellants are entitled to appropriate officiating allowance as per the Rules, but they would not be paid salary in the higher pay scale because they have so far not been promoted as CDPOs.
